parsed.rationale: V1–V4 show QS complexes with poor R-wave progression, which points to an anterior infarct, but the J-point elevation in V2–V3 doesn't clearly reach STEMI thresholds (≥2 mm in men ≥40, ≥1.5 mm in women) on visual inspection and the T waves are upright, so the tracing looks more like an established or age-undetermined anterior MI than a definite acute STEMI. Your team's reading doesn't change that assessment, though baseline noise in the limb leads limits certainty, and clinical correlation, serial ECGs and troponin are needed.
